lastCompletedStory.title: Stage, verify, then atomically rename in build-release.sh --install, and make the docs match

nextStoryContext:
build-release.sh's --install branch now mirrors install.sh's ADR-0058 pattern: per NAME (gateship, gship), STAGED="$(mktemp "${DEST_DIR}/.${NAME}.XXXXXX")", cp HOST_BIN -> STAGED, xattr -cr STAGED, codesign --force --sign - STAGED, codesign -v STAGED (abort on failure), chmod +x STAGED, SMOKE_ACTUAL="$("${STAGED}" --version)" compared to EXPECTED (abort on mismatch), only then mv -f STAGED DEST and STAGED="". No step targets ${DEST} except the final mv. The pre-existing single EXIT trap (originally only 'rm -rf "${SMOKE_DIR:-}"', guarding the earlier hermetic init smoke tmpdir) was extended IN PLACE to 'rm -rf "${SMOKE_DIR:-}" ${STAGED:+"${STAGED}"}' EXIT -- never joined by a second trap on EXIT (that would silently replace the first and stop cleaning SMOKE_DIR). STAGED="" is declared once, right before that trap line, so the ${STAGED:+...} guard is always defined even before the --install branch runs.

test/build-release-smoke.test.ts gained a new describe block ('atomic rename' in its name, so `-t 'atomic rename'` runs only these six tests) that derives every step's position via loopText.indexOf(...) at read time (never a frozen line number: no toBeLessThan(<literal>) anywhere in the block) and asserts each of cp/xattr/codesign-sign/codesign-verify/chmod/version-smoke precedes the mv -f rename, plus a dedicated assertion that the two failure branches (codesign verification failed, --version mismatch) both sit before the mv -- the deliberate consequence (failed verification leaves the prior install intact) is asserted, not left implicit. The script path is now resolved via `process.env.GATESHIP_TEST_BUILD_RELEASE_SH || resolve(...)` (mirrors install.sh's GATESHIP_TEST_INSTALL_SH from CAM-460), swept red-against-main and confirmed: 1 pass / 5 fail when pointed at main's copy. The PRE-EXISTING trap-text assertion at the top of the file (CAM-15 hermetic-init describe block) had to be updated in the same change to match the extended trap body, or it would have gone red the instant the trap grew a second clause -- same 'audit every existing assertion pinning exact source text before extending that text' lesson as CAM-495's SHA256SUMS work.

README.md's Option B (build-from-source) comment above `./scripts/build-release.sh --install` no longer says 'copies to ~/.local/bin/...'; it now says 'verified, then renamed into place at ~/.local/bin/... via atomic rename(2)'. The Option B 'system-wide install to /usr/local/bin' `sudo cp` example block was deliberately left untouched (human-run example, explicitly out of scope per AC8). Option A (packaged binary / install.sh) already read correctly going into this story (US-001 landed first).

file-size-budget.json: test/build-release-smoke.test.ts raised 121->189 (gate's actual `content.split('\n').length` count, not `wc -l`), _ref prepended with a dated US-002/CAM-497 note before the prior US-001 entry, staged in the same commit.

Remaining CAM-497 scope not yet touched: none known from this story's notes beyond US-001 (install.sh, already shipped) and US-002 (this story). If a US-003+ exists in prd.json it was not read by this agent (out of the ingestion scope for a single-story worker).

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed rename(2) is atomic when oldpath/newpath share a filesystem (POSIX guarantee: an observer only ever sees the old or new name, never both/neither), and that `mv` uses rename(2) under the hood for same-filesystem moves. STAGED is created via `mktemp "${DEST_DIR}/.${NAME}.XXXXXX"` (same directory as DEST), so `mv -f "${STAGED}" "${DEST}"` is guaranteed same-filesystem and therefore atomic -- matches the behavior ADR-0058 and install.sh (US-001) already rely on; this story reuses the identical primitive on a second script, no new library surface.
